slides.title: OSI Model
content: The OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) Model is a conceptual framework that standardizes network communication into seven layers
It ensures interoperability between different systems and simplifies network design and troubleshooting
Each layer performs a specific function from user interaction to physical data transmission
It is mainly used as a reference model for understanding network architecture

slides.title: OSI Layers Overview
content: Application Layer provides user services like HTTP, FTP, and email
Presentation Layer handles data formatting, encryption, and compression
Session Layer manages communication sessions and synchronization
Transport Layer ensures reliable delivery using TCP or UDP
Network Layer handles routing and logical addressing using IP
Data Link Layer manages error detection and MAC addressing
Physical Layer transmits raw bits using cables or wireless signals

slides.title: TCP/IP Model
content: The TCP/IP Model is a practical networking model used for real-world internet communication
It consists of four layers designed for efficient and flexible data transmission
It ensures communication between devices using standardized protocols like TCP and IP
It is widely used in modern networking systems including the internet

slides.title: TCP/IP Layers
content: Application Layer provides services like web browsing using HTTP, email using SMTP, and file transfer using FTP
Transport Layer ensures reliable or fast delivery using TCP (reliable) and UDP (connectionless)
Internet Layer handles routing and addressing using IP addresses
Network Interface Layer manages physical transmission using Ethernet and Wi-Fi

slides.title: TCP/IP Communication Process
content: Application Layer prepares data such as email or web request
Transport Layer divides data into packets and ensures reliability using TCP or UDP
Internet Layer assigns IP addresses and routes packets across networks
Network Interface Layer converts data into signals and transmits it through physical media

slides.title: OSI vs TCP/IP Model
content: OSI Model has seven layers while TCP/IP Model has four layers
Presentation and Session layers in OSI are combined into the Application layer in TCP/IP
OSI is a conceptual and theoretical model while TCP/IP is practical and widely implemented
Both models use a layered approach to standardize communication and simplify networking
